name: ColorPicker
purpose: Choose a hexadecimal RGB color, optionally with alpha, using editable text, named swatches and a native RGB picker.
description: Hex entry, labeled swatches and the native RGB chooser with optional alpha. Invalid local drafts remain visible and do not change the committed color. A valid draft commits on blur or Enter. The host owns contrast evaluation, palette policy, theme mapping and persistence.

props.name: value
props.description: Canonical RGB/RGBA hex; shorthand hex is also accepted.

guidance.overview: Choose a hexadecimal RGB color, optionally with alpha, using editable text, named swatches and a native RGB picker.
usage: Accept #RGB/#RRGGBB, plus #RGBA/#RRGGBBAA only when alpha is enabled. Canonicalize accepted values to uppercase six/eight hex digits; RGB with alpha enabled receives FF. Reject unsupported committed values and swatches rather than evaluating arbitrary CSS.

Keep incomplete/invalid editable draft locally without replacing the committed color; expose parse feedback and aria-invalid. A valid changed draft commits on blur or non-composing Enter. Host controlled value changes replace stale drafts.

The native color picker edits RGB only and preserves the current alpha. Optional NumberInput maps a clamped 0–100 percentage to a rounded 8-bit alpha channel; this quantization is explicit, not arbitrary precision.
Render named actual Buttons with pressed state and safe decorative chips. The chip background is validated user-provided hexadecimal data; nested shared controls retain their own styling tokens.

Keep the optional form name on the hex text input only. Its native pattern blocks unsupported drafts on native validated submission. Auxiliary RGB and opacity controls have no duplicate name; opacity has a separate id inside Field.
accessibility: Supply a visible label or enclosing Field. Placeholder text is not an accessible name.
Keep native semantics and keyboard focus; use Field for host descriptions and useful error feedback.
intent: Own palette policy, contrast evaluation, accessible color combinations, theme token mapping, persistence and consistent controlled alpha configuration. A parseable color is not an accessible theme certification.
context: RGB hexadecimal only; no HSL/HSV/Lab/OKLCH gamut tools, eyedropper or gradient editing. The browser owns the native chooser UI.
Invalid draft text stays on the named input until corrected; host code that bypasses native validation must validate its payload. Disabling alpha requires a compatible RGB controlled value.
